_comment: Flash 1 (issue #27, patches/ff_counter/): read the patch's counter block
plus the context the bench procedure asks for.
patches/ff_counter/test/procedure.md sections 1-4 is the full procedure;
this file is only the variable list it needs.
UPDATED 2026-09-22 (brief F1, issues #27 / #44).  Flash 1 now hooks the
10 ms raster of BOTH task sets - 0x432940 in set A (ON-CHIP flash) and
0x12067C in set B - and records which one ran, so the block gained a byte:
The four addresses come from patches/ff_counter/patch.json build.ram
(0x7FFB00, 0x100 B, the block re/findings/ram.md section 8.1 recommends):
+0x00 u32 ff_ticks     activations of the live 10 ms raster since power-up
+0x04 u16 ff_alive     0xFC01 = 64513 once our code has run
+0x06 u8  ff_src_seen  1 = task set A, 2 = task set B, 3 = both
+0x07 u8  ff_reserved  always 0
READ THEM OUT OF patch.json, not out of this file, the day the block moves;
`med9log.py log --patch patches/ff_counter/patch.json` does exactly that
and overrides the four addresses below.
python3 logging/med9log.py log --session logging/sessions/flash1_counter.json \
--patch patches/ff_counter/patch.json --bus gs_usb:0 --seconds 70 \
-o logs/2026-xx-xx_flash1.csv
Checks, in order.  The full decision table - every combination of the
stock raster counters, the Flash 0 on-chip read-back and the slope - is
procedure.md section 4 rows A-I; this is the short form:
1. ff_alive == 64513 and ff_src_seen in {1, 2, 3}.  Both task sets are
hooked, so ff_alive == 0 is now a statement about the FLASH, not
about the task sets: it means neither word executed.  Which of the
two reasons applies is decided by the Flash 0 read-back of
0x404000-0x47FFFF (re/findings/flash_programming.md section 7.2):
stock bytes there -> KESS skipped the on-chip array, so the set-A
word was never written, and because set A is the live set
(scheduler.md 11.8) the external set-B word never runs either ->
procedure.md row D.  Bytes written and still nothing ran -> row E:
stop and investigate before any other flash.
2. ff_src_seen says which set is live, from ONE sample: 1 = set A, which
is what scheduler.md 11.8 predicts (VERIFIED-STATIC); 2 = set B,
which contradicts 11.8 and must be reported loudly (row B); 3 = both
sets run (row C), and then the slope is about 200/s, not 100/s.
Cross-check it against raster_setA_10ms_count / raster_setB_10ms_count
below: exactly one of those two must be moving, and it must be the
one ff_src_seen names.
3. ff_ticks rises monotonically; a single sample can tear in its low
byte, so fit a line over many samples rather than trusting two.
4. The slope is about 100 counts/s: both hooked tasks are 10 ms rasters
(brief C4; scheduler.md sections 11-12; C3 first wrote 10/s here from
section 5.4, and C4 measured 1 ms = 3508 Time Base ticks of 285 ns).
Keep C1's +-2 % tolerance.  Expect every rate about 0.25 % LOW,
because the OS truncates the 285.714 ns tick to 285 ns.  ff_ticks
must track the live set's 10 ms counter 1:1.
5. after a power cycle ff_ticks restarts near 0, ff_alive is 0xFC01 and
ff_src_seen is re-derived from scratch (the cold-start path clears it).
Record the same variables on the STOCK image first - twice - : that
baseline and the Flash-1 log are what tools/logcmp.py compares with
patches/ff_counter/test/tolerance.json, and two runs are what turn its
predicted limits into measured repeatability.

vars.name: ff_ticks
vars.notes: u32 activations of the live 10 ms raster since power-up

vars.name: ff_src_seen
vars.notes: which hook has run: 1 = set A (0x432940, on-chip), 2 = set B (0x12067C), 3 = both. Answers re/findings/scheduler.md 11.7/11.8 from one sample

vars.name: ff_reserved
vars.notes: always 0; a non-zero value means something else writes the block

vars.name: raster_setA_10ms_count
vars.notes: set A 10 ms epilogue (0x4328C8), the stock counter of the task our set-A hook sits in. scheduler.md 11.8 predicts THIS one moves: ff_ticks must then track it 1:1 with ff_src_seen = 1

vars.name: raster_setB_10ms_count
vars.source: re/symbols.csv (C3, address+width); period from scheduler.md sections 11-12 (C4)
vars.notes: set B 10 ms epilogue (0x120570), the stock counter of the task our set-B hook sits in; if THIS one moves instead, ff_src_seen must be 2 and scheduler.md 11.8 is wrong

vars.name: raster_setA_1ms_count
vars.notes: set A 1 ms epilogue; +1000/s if set A is live

vars.name: raster_setB_1ms_count
vars.source: re/symbols.csv (C3, address+width); period from scheduler.md sections 11-12 (C4)
vars.notes: set B 1 ms epilogue (0x11EBDC); +1000/s, the time reference

vars.name: raster_setB_2ms_count
vars.source: re/symbols.csv (C3, address+width); period from scheduler.md sections 11-12 (C4)
